results.question: What warning text is required for a product that contains a button or coin cell battery?
results.reference_answer: The product, its packaging and the listing must carry the ingestion hazard warning: "WARNING: INGESTION HAZARD - This product contains a button or coin cell battery. Swallowing can lead to chemical burns, perforation of soft tissue, and death. Seek immediate medical attention." The warning must also say to keep batteries out of reach of children and to dispose of used batteries immediately.
results.answer: Products containing a button or coin cell battery must carry a specific warning stating that ingestion is a hazard, swallowing can lead to chemical burns, soft tissue perforation, and death, and that immediate medical attention should be sought. The warning must also state to keep batteries out of reach of children and to dispose of used batteries immediately.

The warning shall also state to keep batteries out of reach of children and to dispose of

results.question: What is the maximum concentration of lead allowed in an accessible material of a children's product?
results.reference_answer: Lead must not exceed 0.009 percent by weight in any accessible material of a product intended for children. Concentration limits are expressed as a weight percentage of the homogeneous material, not of the finished article.
results.answer: Lead shall not exceed 0.009 percent by weight in any accessible material of a product intended for children.

intended for children. Cadmium shall not exceed 0.01 percent in plastic materials.
Mercury is prohibited in consumer articles other than as specified in a lighting or
measuring device exemption.

Restricted Substances in Electrical and Electronic Equipment > 1. Hazardous Substance Limits > RSR-004-C1 Restricted Substances and Maximum Concentrations

In homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment the following maximum
concentration values by weight apply: lead 0.1 percent, mercury 0.1 percent, cadmium
0.01 percent, hexavalent chromium 0.1 percent, polybrominated biphenyls 0.1 percent,
polybrominated diphenyl ethers 0.1 percent, and each of DEHP, BBP, DBP, and DIBP 0.1
percent.

Restricted Substances in Food-Contact Materials and Toys > 2. Toys > RSR-005-C6 Element Migration Limits

Migration from toy materials shall not exceed the limits for the 19 regulated elements.
The limits differ by material class: dry brittle powdery or pliable material, liquid or
sticky material, and scraped-off material. Scraped-off material carries the strictest
limits, for example 2.0 milligrams per kilogram for lead.

Home, Garden and Household Chemicals Category Guideline > 3. Specific Restrictions > CAT-006-C10 Concentration Limits

Restricted and Prohibited Substances in Cosmetics > 2. Concentration-Limited Substances > RSR-002-C6 Salicylic Acid

Salicylic acid is limited to 3 percent in rinse-off hair products and 2 percent in other
products, and is prohibited in products for children under 3 years except in shampoos.

results.question: What is the concentration limit for the sum of DEHP, DBP and BBP in plasticised material?
results.reference_answer: The sum of the restricted phthalates DEHP, DBP and BBP must not exceed 0.1 percent by weight in any plasticised material. In toys and childcare articles that can be placed in the mouth, DINP, DIDP and DNOP are restricted to the same limit.
results.answer: The sum of the restricted phthalates DEHP, DBP, and BBP shall not exceed 0.1 percent by weight in any plasticised material.

results.question: What is the chromium VI limit in leather that touches the skin?
results.reference_answer: Chromium VI must not exceed 3 milligrams per kilogram in leather articles in contact with the skin. The limit applies to footwear linings, straps and leather garments.
results.answer: Chromium VI shall not exceed 3 milligrams per kilogram in leather articles in contact with the skin.

In homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment the following maximum

results.question: What is the magnetic flux index threshold above which a loose magnet is prohibited in a toy?
results.reference_answer: A loose or detachable magnet, or a magnetic component that is a small part, must not have a magnetic flux index of 50 kG2mm2 or greater. Products exceeding this threshold are prohibited in toys and in novelty products marketed to any age group.
results.answer: A loose or detachable magnet, or a magnetic component that is a small part, shall not have a magnetic flux index of 50 kG²mm² or greater.
retrieved_texts:

A loose or detachable magnet, or a magnetic component that is a small part, shall not
have a magnetic flux index of 50 kG²mm² or greater. Products exceeding this threshold
are prohibited in toys and in novelty products marketed to any age group.

Toys and Juvenile Products Category Guideline > 3. Safety Labelling > CAT-003-C6 Magnet Hazard

Toys containing loose or detachable magnets exceeding the magnetic flux threshold in
SAF-002-C6 are prohibited for users under 14 and require the ingestion hazard warning
where permitted at all.

Toys and Juvenile Products Category Guideline > 2. Mandatory Category Attributes > CAT-003-C3 Required Attributes

results.question: What are the dimensions of the small parts cylinder?
results.reference_answer: A small part is any component, including one that detaches under the standard use and abuse tests, that fits entirely within a cylinder of 31.7 millimetres diameter and 57.1 millimetres depth measured at the shallowest point.
results.answer: The small parts cylinder has a diameter of 31.7 millimetres and a depth of 57.1 millimetres measured at the shallowest point.

results.question: Can I put 'free shipping' and 'best seller' in my product name?
results.reference_answer: No. Titles must not contain promotional claims, price references, shipping terms or urgency language. "free shipping" and "best seller" are both given as prohibited examples. Promotional language in a title is a Tier 1 defect and suppresses the listing from search.
results.answer: You cannot include promotional claims such as "free shipping" or "best seller" in your product titles, as titles must not contain promotional claims, price references, shipping terms, or urgency language.
retrieved_texts:
Product Title and Naming Standards > 3. Prohibited Title Content > CLS-001-C6 Promotional and Marketing Language

Titles shall not contain promotional claims, price references, shipping terms, or
urgency language. Prohibited examples include "free shipping", "best seller",
"sale now", "limited stock", "cheapest", and "100% guaranteed". Detection of
promotional language is a Tier 1 defect and suppresses the listing from search.

Product Title and Naming Standards > 3. Prohibited Title Content > CLS-001-C7 Seller Identity and Contact Details

Titles shall not include the seller's store name, website address, email address,
telephone number, or any off-platform contact instruction. This is a Tier 1 defect and
triggers immediate listing suppression pending seller correction.

Substance Disclosure Obligations and Restricted Marketing Claims > 2. Restricted Marketing Claims > RSR-006-C4 Free-From Claims

"Free from" claims are permitted only where the substance is genuinely absent, the
substance is one a buyer could reasonably expect to be present, and the claim does not
imply that products containing the substance are unsafe when they are lawfully
compliant. "Chemical-free" is prohibited in all cases.

Primary Product Image Standards > 3. Prohibited Overlays > IMG-001-C7 No Text or Graphic Overlays

The primary image shall not contain text, logos, watermarks, borders, badges, colour
blocks, price flashes, promotional banners, or seller branding. Text that appears
physically on the product or its packaging is permitted.

Product Description and Bullet Feature Standards > 4. Claims Discipline > CLS-002-C9 Prohibited Absolute Claims

Unqualified absolute claims are prohibited in the description. Prohibited forms include
"cures", "prevents disease", "100% safe", "non-toxic" without a standard reference, and
"eco-friendly" without a named certification scheme.

results.question: Is it okay for a face cream listing to say the product cures acne?
results.reference_answer: No. A cosmetic may claim to cleanse, perfume, change appearance, protect or keep in good condition, but claims to treat, heal or prevent a medical condition reclassify the product as a medicine and are prohibited in the cosmetics category. "cures acne" is listed explicitly as a prohibited claim.
results.answer: Claims that a product cures acne are explicitly prohibited.
retrieved_texts:
Cosmetics and Personal Care Category Guideline > 3. Claims > CAT-005-C8 Prohibited Claim Examples

The following are prohibited: "cures acne", "removes wrinkles permanently",
"anti-bacterial" without a biocidal authorisation, "SPF 100+", "reverses hair loss", and
"dermatologist prescribed".

Cosmetics and Personal Care Category Guideline > 3. Claims > CAT-005-C7 Cosmetic Versus Medicinal Boundary

A cosmetic may claim to cleanse, perfume, change appearance, protect, or keep in good
condition. Claims to treat, heal, or prevent a medical condition reclassify the product
as a medicine and are prohibited in this category.

Cosmetics and Personal Care Category Guideline > 3. Claims > CAT-005-C10 Restricted Cosmetic Ingredients

Ingredients restricted under RSR-002, including hydroquinone, mercury compounds, and
specified corticosteroids, are prohibited in cosmetics regardless of concentration
unless an explicit exemption is recorded in RSR-002.

Restricted and Prohibited Substances in Cosmetics > 1. Prohibited Substances > RSR-002-C2 Skin-Lightening Products

Skin-lightening products are a high-risk sub-category. Every listing requires a test
report under RSR-001-C8 covering mercury, hydroquinone, and corticosteroids before
approval is granted.

Restricted and Prohibited Substances in Cosmetics > 3. Allergens and Labelling > RSR-002-C10 Animal Testing

Products tested on animals for cosmetic purposes after the storefront jurisdiction's
cut-off date may not be listed, and any cruelty-free claim requires a named certification
scheme under CLS-002-C9.

results.question: A seller wants to sell a toy with tiny pieces to two year olds. Is that allowed?
results.reference_answer: No. A toy intended for children under 36 months must not contain, and must not be capable of generating, a small part, and may not be listed for that age group. This is an absolute prohibition rather than a labelling obligation, so a warning does not make it permissible.
results.answer: A toy intended for children under 36 months must not contain or be capable of generating a small part, and it may not be listed for that age group. This is an absolute prohibition.
retrieved_texts:

A toy intended for children under 36 months shall not contain, and shall not be capable
of generating, a small part. Such a product may not be listed for that age group. This
is an absolute prohibition, not a labelling obligation.

Toys and Juvenile Products Category Guideline > 3. Safety Labelling > CAT-003-C5 Small Parts Warning

Any toy intended for children under 36 months that contains or can generate a small part
shall not be listed for that age group. Where the toy is intended for children over 36
months and contains small parts, the listing shall display the choking hazard warning

accompanying label image.

Choking, Ingestion and Mechanical Hazard Labeling Requirements > 1. Small Parts > SAF-002-C3 Over 36 Months Labelling Obligation

A toy intended for children of 36 months and over that contains a small part shall carry

Restricted Substances in Food-Contact Materials and Toys > 2. Toys > RSR-005-C9 Nitrosamines

Nitrosamines and nitrosatable substances shall not be present above 0.05 and 1

results.question: What do I need to show buyers about what is inside a shampoo?
results.reference_answer: Every cosmetic listing must publish the complete ingredient list using the international nomenclature, in descending order of weight, with ingredients below one percent permitted in any order after that threshold. An incomplete or paraphrased list is a Tier 1 labelling defect. A legible unretouched image of the physical ingredient panel is also required.
results.answer: For a cosmetic listing such as a shampoo, you must publish the complete ingredient list using the international nomenclature in descending order of weight, with ingredients below one percent permitted in any order after the one percent threshold. You must individually name the 26 designated fragrance allergens if they are present above 0.001 percent in leave-on products or 0.01 percent in rinse-off products, and identify ingredients present in nanoform with the suffix "(nano)". Additionally, you must include a sharp, legible, unretouched image of the physical ingredient list.
retrieved_texts:

Every cosmetic listing shall publish the complete ingredient list using the
international nomenclature, in descending order of weight, with ingredients below one

paraphrased ingredient list is a Tier 1 labelling defect.

Restricted and Prohibited Substances in Cosmetics > 3. Allergens and Labelling > RSR-002-C7 Fragrance Allergen Declaration

The 26 designated fragrance allergens shall be named individually in the ingredient list
where present above 0.001 percent in leave-on products or 0.01 percent in rinse-off
products.

Restricted and Prohibited Substances in Cosmetics > 3. Allergens and Labelling > RSR-002-C9 Nanomaterials

Ingredients present in nanoform shall be identified in the ingredient list with the
suffix "(nano)".

Cosmetics and Personal Care Category Guideline > 2. Mandatory Labelling > CAT-005-C6 Warning Statements

Where the product requires a statutory warning — for example hair dyes requiring the

Category-Specific Image Requirements > 2. Food, Supplements and Cosmetics > IMG-004-C3 Ingredient and Nutrition Panel Image

Food, supplement, and cosmetic listings shall include a sharp, legible, unretouched image
of the physical ingredient list and, for food, the nutrition panel. This image is
mandatory and its absence causes suppression under CAT-004-C5 and CAT-005-C3.

results.question: For a children's toy that contains both magnets and a coin cell battery, what warnings do I need on the listing, and what is the lead limit for the materials?
results.reference_answer: Three requirements apply. For magnets, where they are permitted at all, the listing must warn that swallowing more than one magnet may cause serious or fatal internal injury and that immediate medical attention is required; a loose magnet at or above 50 kG2mm2 flux index is prohibited outright. For the coin cell, the ingestion hazard warning is required on the product, packaging and listing, and the compartment must be tool-secured or need two simultaneous movements to open. For materials, lead must not exceed 0.009 percent by weight in any accessible material of a children's product.
results.answer: For the listing of a toy containing a coin cell battery, you must carry the warning stating that ingestion is a hazard, that swallowing can lead to chemical burns, soft tissue perforation, and death, and that you should seek immediate medical attention, keep batteries out of reach of children, and dispose of used batteries immediately. The context does not mention any lead limit for the materials.

regardless of the primary category.

These clauses apply to any consumer product containing a button or coin cell of 32

results.question: I'm listing a mains-powered LED lamp imported from another country. What approval do I need and what must I tell buyers about the plug?
results.reference_answer: Any product with a mains connection requires the electrical goods category approval, and the approval application must include the plug and adapter specification for each storefront the product will be sold into. Where the supplied plug does not match the destination storefront's socket standard, the listing must state this prominently in the first bullet feature and state whether an adapter is included; omitting it is a Tier 1 safety-labelling defect.
results.answer: Mains-powered products require the electrical goods category approval described in CLS-006-C4, with an application that includes the plug and adapter specification for each storefront. Additionally, if the supplied plug does not match the destination storefront's socket standard, the listing must prominently state this in the first bullet feature and state whether an adapter is included.

jurisdiction and shall reference the applicable safety standard in the compliance
attributes.

Consumer Electronics Category Guideline > 3. Electrical Safety > CAT-001-C5 Mains-Powered Product Approval

Any product with a mains connection requires the electrical goods category approval

Battery and Electrical Safety Labeling Requirements > 3. Mains Electrical Safety > SAF-003-C10 Charger and Adapter Requirements

Supplied chargers shall bear the conformity marking, shall declare output voltage and

Products shall declare their insulation class and, where marketed for outdoor or

results.question: What allergen information must a packaged food listing show, and what image is required to go with it?

Omitting a present allergen is a Tier 1 safety defect causing immediate suppression. A legible image of the physical ingredient and nutrition panel is a mandatory secondary image, and listings without it are suppressed.
results.answer: A food listing must declare every regulated allergen present, including allergens present through cross-contamination where the manufacturer declares a precautionary statement. instructions, and the shelf-life or best-before basis.

results.question: For children's pyjamas, what flammability rule applies and how does it have to appear on the listing?
results.reference_answer: Children's nightwear must either meet the low-flammability performance requirement of the applicable standard or, where it does not, carry the permanent warning label "KEEP AWAY FROM FIRE". Pyjamas that fail the performance requirement must carry the warning, while nightdresses and dressing gowns that fail it may not be supplied for children at all. Where a garment carries the warning, the listing must reproduce it in the first three bullet features and show the warning label in a secondary image.
results.answer: Children's pyjamas must meet the low-flammability performance requirement or carry the permanent warning label "KEEP AWAY FROM FIRE". If the garment carries a flammability warning, the listing must reproduce the warning in the first three bullet features under SAF-001-C7 and display the warning label in a secondary image.
retrieved_texts:
Flammability Requirements for Textiles and Furnishings > 1. Children's Sleepwear > SAF-005-C2 Performance or Warning

Children's nightwear shall either meet the low-flammability performance requirement of
the applicable standard, or, where it does not, carry the permanent warning label
"KEEP AWAY FROM FIRE". Pyjamas that fail the performance requirement shall carry the
warning; nightdresses and dressing gowns that fail the requirement may not be supplied
for children.

Flammability Requirements for Textiles and Furnishings > 1. Children's Sleepwear > SAF-005-C1 Scope of Sleepwear Rules

These clauses apply to nightdresses, dressing gowns, pyjamas, and bathrobes intended for

Where a garment carries a flammability warning, the listing shall reproduce the warning

results.question: Does holding a category approval mean I no longer have to worry about restricted substance limits?
results.reference_answer: No. A restricted-substance limit applies independently of any category approval, and holding a category approval never waives a limit in the restricted substances series. Where the prohibited and restricted listing policy conflicts with a category guideline, the more restrictive provision applies.
results.answer: Holding a category approval never waives a restricted substance limit. Restricted-substance limits apply independently of category approvals.
retrieved_texts:

Listing Defect Taxonomy and Enforcement Ladder > 1. Defect Tiers > CLS-005-C1 Tier 1 Defects

A Tier 1 defect is one that misleads the buyer, evades platform controls, or creates a
safety or legal exposure. Tier 1 defects result in immediate listing suppression at
detection, without a correction window. Examples include prohibited safety claims,
off-platform diversion, missing hazard labelling, and identifier reuse.

Listing Defect Taxonomy and Enforcement Ladder > 1. Defect Tiers > CLS-005-C2 Tier 2 Defects

A Tier 2 defect degrades catalog quality without misleading the buyer. Tier 2 defects
carry a 14 calendar day correction window before suppression. Examples include
capitalisation violations, missing brand element, and incomplete bullet lists.

Listing Defect Taxonomy and Enforcement Ladder > 2. Enforcement Ladder > CLS-005-C4 First Occurrence

A first Tier 1 or Tier 2 defect on a listing produces a notification to the seller
identifying the clause breached and the required correction.

Listing Defect Taxonomy and Enforcement Ladder > 2. Enforcement Ladder > CLS-005-C6 Systemic Breach

A pattern of the same Tier 1 defect across more than 20 listings is treated as a
systemic breach and may result in category-level selling restriction pending a
remediation plan.

Listing Defect Taxonomy and Enforcement Ladder > 1. Defect Tiers > CLS-005-C3 Tier 3 Defects

A Tier 3 defect is advisory. It generates a dashboard recommendation, does not suppress
the listing, and does not count toward the enforcement ladder. Examples include a title
between 150 and 200 characters and a missing leading attribute label in bullets.

results.question: Can I use an AI-generated image as the main photo for my product?
results.reference_answer: No. Images produced by a generative model may only be used as secondary lifestyle images, must be labelled as illustrative in an on-image caption, and must never be used as the primary image or as a compliance label image. The primary image must be a photograph or a photorealistic render of the actual product supplied.

Primary Product Image Standards > 1. Technical Requirements > IMG-001-C3 Aspect Ratio and Framing

The primary image shall be square or between 1:1 and 4:3. The product shall occupy at
least 85 percent of the image frame.

Primary Product Image Standards > 2. Background and Composition > IMG-001-C6 Product Must Be Real

The primary image shall be a photograph or a photorealistic render of the actual product
supplied. Line drawings, sketches, placeholder graphics, and stock images of a similar
but different product are prohibited.

Primary Product Image Standards > 1. Technical Requirements > IMG-001-C1 Minimum Resolution

The primary image shall be at least 1000 pixels on its longest side. Images below 1000
pixels do not support the zoom viewer and the listing is ineligible for featured
placement. Images below 500 pixels on the longest side are rejected at submission.

Primary Product Image Standards > 1. Technical Requirements > IMG-001-C2 Accepted Formats and File Size

Accepted formats are JPEG, PNG, and WebP. The maximum file size is 10 megabytes. Animated
formats and progressive interlacing are not accepted for the primary image.

Image Authenticity, Manipulation and Generative Content Rules > 3. Renders and Generative Content > IMG-003-C6 Generative AI Imagery

Images produced by a generative model may be used only as secondary lifestyle images,
shall be labelled as illustrative in an on-image caption, and shall never be used as the
primary image or as a compliance label image under IMG-002-C5.
